title: Domain of a Rational Function with a Factored Denominator
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain of y=1/(x^2+x) by excluding the inputs that make the denominator vanish.

steps.title: Set the Denominator Nonzero
steps.explanation: The formula fails only where x^2+x=0, so those points must be removed.
steps.why: Division by zero is undefined and it is the sole restriction here.

steps.title: Factor Completely
steps.explanation: Pull out the common factor x to write the denominator as a product of two linear terms.
steps.why: Factoring turns the quadratic equation into easy first-degree equations.

steps.title: Solve x(x+1)=0
steps.explanation: The product is zero exactly when x=0 or x+1=0, i.e. x=-1.
steps.why: Zero-product property: ab=0 implies a=0 or b=0.

steps.title: State the Domain
steps.explanation: Every real number except -1 and 0 is an admissible input.
steps.why: Two punctures divide the real line into three open intervals.
